steps.action: Opened developer.spotify.com/dashboard in the project browser profile
steps.observation: Redirected to login; the owner signed in. Then the Developer Terms checkbox, and 'verify your email address before you can create an app' (Create app disabled). The owner did all three.

steps.action: Opened the Create app form on a free account
steps.observation: Fields: name*, description*, website, redirect URIs*, API/SDK boxes (Web API greyed out), a Premium upgrade banner, and a Developer Terms and Design Guidelines box the owner ticked.

steps.action: The owner clicked Save; the agent read the app's Basic Information page
steps.observation: The app was created on a free account in Development mode, refresh token lifetime 180 days. The Client ID is shown; the secret is behind 'View client secret' and was not viewed.

steps.action: Added the redirect URI http://127.0.0.1:3000/callback in the form
steps.observation: A loopback address was accepted and listed. The docs say plain localhost is rejected; that was not tested here.

steps.action: Cleanup: the test app was not deleted during the session
steps.observation: The app still exists until the owner deletes it; no secret was ever viewed, so none needs removing. The account also keeps the verified email and accepted terms.

stoppedAt: before viewing the client secret or using the Web API (greyed out on a free account): guide steps 1, 3 and 4 were observed, steps 2 and 5 to 9 were not attempted

corrections.docClaim: A Spotify developer account to create and manage Client IDs in the Spotify dashboard. The captured sources show only that developers manage Client IDs through the dashboard, not the exact sign-up requirements.
corrections.observed: A Spotify account (a free one worked) plus accepting the Developer Terms and a verified email address before Create app turns on. On a free account a Premium banner shows and Web API is greyed out.

corrections.docClaim: New apps run in Development Mode.
corrections.observed: The new app was created in Development mode, with a 180-day refresh token lifetime shown on its page.
